text: I am mindful of the potential influence of misinformation surrounding this conflict.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: There have been various reports of supposed atrocities committed by both sides.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many such reports remain contested and lack independent verification.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is important to acknowledge that there is a possibility that some information might be a product of war propaganda.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: There are significant challenges faced by journalists in independently confirming these allegations, given the hazards of reporting from a conflict zone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: As Singaporeans, it is imperative that we individually take the initiative to guard against the spread of misinformation and disinformation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should not look to the Government to censor fake news for us.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: As an article on the website, Vox, advised, if a video, photo or post about the war makes you immediately furious or upset, refrain from instantly sharing it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Check the source by reviewing the account and its past posts and cross-reference it with reliable news outlets.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will help keep our discourse on this issue rational and focused on what is the most important – the welfare of innocent civilians in Israel and Palestine.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They also provide a crucial pressure release valve for discontent, helping to prevent individuals from becoming overly influenced by extreme rhetoric from foreign sources.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Rather, it could lead to the debate being driven into radicalised corners of the Internet, which is where the real danger lies.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Arguments against greater public debate have often cited concerns about a general lack of understanding surrounding the complex Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What active steps are being taken to deepen Singaporeans' understanding of the conflict?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Are we, as individuals, proactively seeking to educate ourselves on this topic?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: With teachers or facilitators guiding these discussions, the conversations will be kept balanced and will avoid becoming overly contentious.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Despite its complexity, it is essential for each of us to make the effort to understand its nuances so as to foster rational and informed public discussions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While the conflict is miles away from Singapore, we cannot help but mourn the heart-wrenching violence against innocent civilians, including children, on both sides of the conflict.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I echo fellow Parliamentary colleagues who have given their speeches earlier and express my deepest condolences to all innocent victims and civilian casualties and their families.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have been encouraged by the views of some residents I have engaged in my closed-door chats and dialogues with them on this issue in the past week and would like to voice some of their perspectives in Parliament on this Motion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Many of us in the Malay/Muslim community have heavy hearts regarding plight of the Palestine people.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It was reported in the news that some of us are feeling a "real sense of helplessness".

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The community is experiencing difficult emotions, as we hear daily about the powerless Palestinians suffering through the disproportionate, aggressive actions by both parties in the conflict.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is understandable, when they see the news and social media posts, and are disturbed by hospitals and places of worship in Gaza being bombed and destroyed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My residents, both Muslims and non-Muslims, have also shared that there is misinformation spreading on social media and WhatsApp on the conflict.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Worse, I am concerned of divisive voices online using it for incitement or hate speech against other religions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As a Singaporean, I am proud of the way that the outpouring of sympathy for those suffering is largely done in constructively and calmly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should all understand the complex context of the Israel-Palestinian conflict and know the facts, before forwarding such messages to our family members and friends.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope that we can continue to perform supplication and our solat hajat special prayers for peace and alleviation of their suffering.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Bishan-Toa Payoh GRC, mosques such as Masjid Omar Salmah and Masjid Muhajirin have held special prayers on 20 October, following the call of encouragement by MUIS and the Office of the Mufti to conduct recitation of the supplication Qunut Nazilah, as well as special supplication during the Friday sermon and prayers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have attended Friday prayers in which these prayers were done since early October.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MUIS has also worked with Muslim.sg to offer religious guidance on appropriate responses to this conflict and will soon be issuing an irsyad (guidance).

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: During my recent dialogue with a group of Toa Payoh East residents, both young and old, several residents asked how each resident can help in terms of providing donations through the right channels, that is, the mosques, the UN and also how to receive the correct information through the Government.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One resident even asked if we could send our SCDF Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel to conduct search and rescue operation, similar to the help provided in response to the Türkiye-Syria earthquake in February this year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I said that we should focus on providing the basic needs like water, food and medical supplies to the civilians in Israel-Gaza.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This clearly demonstrates the compassion and concern of my residents regardless of race or religion for those affected in Gaza, even though an SCDF effort in a war-torn area might not be possible.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I shared that all of us can provide immediate assistance to the Palestinian victims through the various accredited charities that are raising funds for aid to Gaza.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In English) I will now speak in English, Mr Speaker, on what I hope the Government will do and take next steps.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Despite the difference in views on the issue, all of them found common ground in condemning the use of violence and are concerned with the needless loss of civilian lives, particularly those of children.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To that end, some of these youths have expressed willingness to contribute to numerous calls for aid within the community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Similar to the feedback raised by my Muslim residents, the youths also brought up a few points of concern, chief of which is the influence of media, both traditional and social media.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that different media channels seem to report different aspects of the conflict and, sometimes, with a subjective spin.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such is evident in the various feedback I have gathered, where I enquired about how opinions are formed and what the source of their information is.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is important as false information has dire consequences for the unity of our country and how we function as a nation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad that the Singapore Government has voted to support the resolution on the "Protection of Civilians and Upholding Legal and Humanitarian Obligations" at the Emergency Special Session of the UN General Assembly on 27 October while also condemning unequivocally the acts of terror and abhorrent deeds that parties in the conflict have done and which cannot be justified by any rationale whatsoever.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As a society, we must embrace the principles behind which Singapore supported the resolution, most importantly, that all innocent civilian lives on both sides of the conflict must be protected.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I hope the Government can update the House on what further measures, such as in the realm of diplomacy, that Singapore is taking to expedite the protection of innocent civilian lives and the provision of humanitarian assistance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I refer to the Arab Barometer survey of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza in early October this year, where the majority of Gazans surveyed also favoured a two-state solution.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A former Prime Minister of the Palestinian Authority, Salam Fayyad, has suggested in an article published in the Foreign Affairs magazine on 27 October, that the way ahead for peace would include formal Israeli recognition of the Palestinians' right to a sovereign state on Israeli-occupied territory.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Most crucially, he has suggested for these to be underpinned by an ironclad mutual commitment to non-violence.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Singapore Government can share its further plans to support the international community's efforts to broker a just and lasting peace between the parties involved.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Before I end, I would like to speak a bit on the economic ramifications for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The impact of a protracted conflict in Gaza, and if it spreads or worsens, will have economic and financial ramifications globally.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As it stands now, the Israel-Hamas conflict adds another layer of complexity to the geopolitics of the world and existing economic headwinds.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Though it is still early to raise concern about global output effects, there are key risks for global energy and key commodity prices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: All these will lead to negative externalities and impact on prices here in Singapore in no time, even though it is so far away from us at the moment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, it is in our interest too to ensure this conflict is not prolonged, not just importantly to save innocent lives, but also to protect the welfare of Singaporeans going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank the Singapore Cabinet and the Government for taking a principled stand on this issue and for supporting the resolution on the "Protection of Civilians and Upholding Legal and Humanitarian Obligations" at the Emergency Special Session of the UN General Assembly on 27 October.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It bodes well for Singapore and it is not an easy decision but I would like to say thank you.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should also provide aid where we can, via the right channels, and I hope the authorities can help guide on these next steps.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But most importantly, I urge all efforts to ensure that all innocent civilians, especially the children, must be protected.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am confident that Singaporeans will continue to be resilient and harmonious in the face of these issues and band together to help those in need, as we weather any global geo-political and economic storms ahead.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Like many Singaporeans, the PSP is distressed and saddened by the tragic violence and loss of life in Israel and the Gaza Strip since Hamas launched its attacks in Southern Israel on 7 October 2023 and the subsequent retaliatory military actions taken by Israel.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We unequivocally condemn the violence committed by both sides against innocent civilians, especially women and children.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We call on Israel to comply with international law, including the Geneva Conventions and the UN Charter.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Israel must not collectively punish a captive civilian population, nearly half of which are children and teenagers under age 18, in the Gaza Strip.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Israel must immediately rescind its order for Palestinian civilians, which includes gravely sick patients in hospitals, and UN staff to evacuate from northern Gaza Strip to southern Gaza Strip.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: More than a million Palestinians in Gaza have been internally displaced by the recent conflict.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This internal displacement must not be allowed to evolve into a repeat of the Nakba in 1948, when 700,000 Palestinians were permanently displaced from their towns and villages.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must prevent the Palestinians in Gaza from being permanently displaced to Egypt or any other nation.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even before the recent events, the living conditions in Gaza have been difficult for the Palestinians.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Israel must immediately allow all humanitarian aid to be delivered into Gaza and fully restore civilian access to fuel, food, water, medical aid and other basic necessities.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict is a long-standing and complex issue dating back to and beyond the formation of the state of Israel in 1948.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will help to reduce the risk of Singaporeans being swayed by biased, inaccurate or one-sided emotional discourse, which we have seen on both traditional and social media platforms.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We urge Singaporeans from all communities to be mindful of what we say and do regarding this issue, especially on online forums.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We all have the responsibility to refrain from engaging in inflammatory rhetoric that could threaten the peace and harmony that we enjoy in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We call on all Singaporeans to report any signs of potential radicalisation to the authorities.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In line with this, PSP rejects any attempts by foreign players to influence Singaporeans or dictate to Singapore what could be done in relation to this conflict.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singapore's position on all our foreign policy and domestic issues should be for Singaporeans to decide only.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I begin by expressing my deepest sympathies to the innocent victims affected by this conflict, the loss of lives, particularly children and women, is a tragedy that underscores the urgency of our response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are addressing a matter that deeply troubles our collective conscience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: At a fundamental level, we all recognise that violent extremism is unacceptable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We condemn any ideas or action of individuals or groups who endorse or resort to violence to accomplish thei ideological, religious or political objectives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This includes terrorism and vasrious other types of violence driven by politics or community factors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: These concepts play a significant role in international relation and have a direct impact on the public safety and security of a nation like Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Solidarity refers to the unity, cooperation and support among individuals, groups or nation, especially in times of adversity or when addressing common challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is the sense of shared responsibility and a commitment to working together to achieve common goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The sentiments of our public cannot be ignored.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The loss of innocent children, women and civilians in conflict touches the hearts of people worldwide, including Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is our duty to represent their concerns on the international stage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Security in the context of a nation like Singapore encompasses both national and international security.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: National security refers to the protection of a country's autonomy, territorial integrity and the safety of our citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: International security, on the other hand, focuses on maintaining peace and stability between nations and preventing conflicts that could have global repercussions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our commitment to international security and peace is not only a moral duty but a critical step in safeguarding our own nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: By supporting this Motion, we stand firmly against acts of violence and the violation of international laws.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Terrorism can never be justified and it is our collective duty to condemn this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In this conflict, we must insist that all parties involved prioritise the safe and security of civilians, release all hostages and minimise the effects of combat on the civilian population.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our racial and religious harmony is one of our greatest strengths and something we must cherish and protect at all costs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Ensuring global security and stability is integral to preserving our racial harmony.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our support for peaceful resolution reflects our commitment to maintaining a world where all nationalities, cultures and religions can strive together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In terms of the security of our nation, we must remain vigilant and proactive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This entails monitoring, intelligence sharing, community engagement and a strong commitment to countering extremism.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is vital for Singapore to come together irrespective of differences to build a resilient and united front against division, violence and terrorism.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: By doing so, we can collectively mitigate risks, promote peace and protect our shared values and way of life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Peace is the absence of violence, conflict and the presence of harmony and cooperation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Peace is essential for the stability and prosperity of our nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The situation in Gaza is not merely theoretical or a distant concern.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is directly connected to our racial harmony, our duty to prevent potential security threats and our commitment to voicing the concerns of the general public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our support for peace and the condemnation of acts of terror resonate not only on the international stage but within our own border.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As we reflect on this crisis, let us remember the value of solidarity, security and peace to our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This conflict occurs thousands of kilometres away and has a long, complicated and often violent history going back thousands of years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But all Singaporeans are horrified, are saddened by this latest escalation of the Israel-Hamas conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Anyone with a heart must feel pain when we witness the suffering of fellow human beings – regardless of race, language, religion, ideology or allegiance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Early in the morning of 7 October 2023, Hamas launched several thousand rockets into Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The victims included innocent civilians at home, many of them asleep, young people attending a concert and several of our fellow ASEAN nationals working on farms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It was not a military operation, targeted at military targets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Such acts cannot be justified by any rationale, any historical grievance, any religious belief, any context.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is in our absolute national interest to hold fast to this stand, not just because we feel sorry for innocent victims, but because our national interests are at stake.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore must take a clear and unambiguous stand against terrorism in all circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I was somewhat reassured when I listened to the Leader of the Opposition's speech just now, where he now seems to have clarified that the attack that was launched by Hamas was not simply a military operation, but in fact, deserves to be condemned.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Mr Gerald Giam was even more specific.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think you used the word "unequivocally condemn" the attacks by Hamas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I could not help noticing that both Members of the WP were unable to use the word terrorism, I will leave that for you to clarify later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I must share with you that when I first saw your published statement, it left room for ambiguity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think your speeches in this Chamber today are more reassuring, but I would feel even better if you can clearly and unequivocally say indiscriminate attacks on civilians, on women, on children and taking hostages is a clear and present act of terror, and say that for the sake of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These attacks have obviously deeply shaken the Israelis' sense of safety and security.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We now know that Israel has responded by launching an intensive aerial bombardment on Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It imposed a blockade on the delivery of food, water and fuel supplies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On 28 October, Israeli troops expanded their ground operations in Gaza to destroy Hamas' military capacity and its vast network of underground tunnels, much of which, it is alleged, is located under civilian infrastructure, including schools and hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Israel's intensive bombardment and blockade has caused a massive humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the 10th UN General Assembly Emergency Special Session on 27 October 2023, Singapore voted for a humanitarian truce so that immediate and sustained humanitarian provision of essential supplies and services to civilians throughout the Gaza Strip can be provided.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Members have a copy of that resolution that we voted for, including the explanation of vote by our Permanent Representative, Mr Burhan Gafoor, which again, made the point that there were glaring omissions in that resolution, to call out Hamas for conducting an act of terror and for not acknowledging the right of self-defence on the part of Israel, which I will explain a little bit more later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, Singapore must and must always take a zero-tolerance approach towards terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to be categorical in rejecting terrorism, whoever, whenever, wherever it is perpetrated.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And as I said just now, we do so not just out of sympathy, but because terrorism is a clear and present danger and threat for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second, international law dictates that all states have the legitimate and inherent right to defend themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is enshrined in Article 51 of the UN Charter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I do not think I need to remind this House that this is a very important principle for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Have no doubt – if Singapore is ever attacked, we would certainly assert and exercise the right of self-defence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, all countries must ensure that if military action is taken in exercising this right of self-defence, they must abide by the principles of necessity and proportionality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They must also comply with the laws of war, including the principle of distinction and humanity enshrined in the Geneva Conventions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In such times like this, it is crucial that decisions are not made out of anger, blind wrath and hatred, but are made in line with moral values and legal principles that shape our common humanity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In a jointly written Financial Times commentary last month, a group of distinguished Jewish jurists – and these include experts in international humanitarian law – they strongly counselled Israel and its leaders to act in a restrained and thoughtful way that would not make the country's problems worse.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One of these jurists, in fact, included Lord David Neuberger, who was the former President of the Supreme Court of the UK.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Equally, international law requires combatants to ensure minimum destruction to civilian life and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: An intent to cause indiscriminate damage, rather than behaving in a precise manner to minimise damage would, if established, constitute a grave violation of international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the conduct of any military campaign, politicians and commanders alike must be careful to ensure that their words do not imply to their troops that the laws of war can be disregarded, nor employ language whose effect is to dehumanise a civilian population." I want to emphasise that last sentence, "to dehumanise a civilian population", because usually, that is a very clear indication that conflict between countries, states or civilisations is about to begin.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And the moment that human beings can dehumanise the other is the time when unspeakable horror, barbarity and terrorism is conducted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Member of Parliament, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim had asked that question earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Yes, we will support the investigation of all allegations after the war in accordance with international law and we hope that all parties will cooperate in these investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: History will judge each party's response not only by whether and how immediate threats are resolved, but also by the effects on the long-term stability and security of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fourth, humanitarian assistance must reach the affected civilian populations immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why we call on all parties to enable this, particularly, Israel and Egypt which have immediate borders with Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Yesterday, I spoke to the Egyptian Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I told him Singapore understands the tremendous strain that Egypt, as an immediate neighbour, faces.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I said we want to support you, we have our people in Singapore who care, we are raising funds, and let us know how we can assist Egypt.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I commended the Egyptian government's efforts to open the Rafah crossing to facilitate the flow of humanitarian goods into Gaza, and equally, the possible evacuation of seriously injured persons for medical treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The day before, I had spoken to the Foreign Minister of the UAE, who was also trying to work out plans, perhaps, to evacuate injured children and their families for treatment elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We strongly support all these efforts by their immediate neighbours, as well as by the UN and all the other relief organisations to increase aid to Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Members are all aware that the Singapore Government contributed seed funding of about $300,000 to the Singapore Red Cross, which is working with its partners to support the relief efforts in Gaza and working closely with the Palestine Red Crescent Society, the Egyptian Red Crescent Society.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, right now, I think Singaporeans have donated nearly $5 million to the fundraising drives by the SRC and the RLAF.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I am sure more will come in in the weeks to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Later tonight, Dr Mohamad Maliki Osman will be leaving.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He will also help to ensure facilitation and that the goodness of the hearts of Singaporeans will be directed through the right channels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He will explain a little bit more after my speech.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have consistently stated for a long time that Israel must accept a Palestinian state, just as Palestinians must also accept Israel's right to exist.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have expressed our firm opposition to violations of international law and to unilateral measures which imperil the prospects for peace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Many of you know that we have got good relations with Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I hope you also know that we have good relations with the Palestinian people and with the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But look at our voting record in the United Nations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During the Six-Day War in 1967, Israeli forces occupied the Old City of Jerusalem and parts of the West Bank after Jordan attacked Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 1967 – some Members of this House were not born yet – following the war, we voted in support of all the UN General Assembly (UNGA) resolutions calling on Israel to rescind unilateral measures taken to change the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also voted in support of UNGA resolutions that reject Israeli settlement activities in the West Bank.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members can also access the handout through the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But good friends also speak truth, even if it is disagreeable and not the most comfortable to the person on the other side.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And our ability to speak truth to friends and to be friends to both sides, even while they are locked in mortal conflict, is a privileged position but one that can only be maintained if we are consistent and we operate on the basis of principles.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Unfortunately, the peace process in both Israel and Palestine – and Members have heard a good synopsis on the history by Mr Vikram Nair in his opening speech, I hope you paid attention to it – but the upshot of that process—first, I would remind all Members that being a peacemaker in the Middle East is dangerous.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When he made peace with Israel in Camp David, I think they signed it in 1978; by 1981, he was assassinated.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In Israel, then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, in fact, was the Israel Defense Force (IDF) Chief-of-Staff during the 1967 war.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a realist, a General, a Commander and a soldier.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Vikram Nair reminded us that it was Mr Yitzhak Rabin and Mr Yasser Arafat who signed the Oslo Accords in 1993, and subsequently a second round in 1995.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, this is what has led to the creation of the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It led to the Israelis pulling out of Gaza.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, as you all would know, Mr Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated in November 1999, not by an Arab, but by an Israeli extremist.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As for the Palestinians, the Palestinian Authority consisted initially of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) because, in fact, the Olso Accords provided, for the first time ever, the PLO recognised Israel's right to exist and the Israelis recognised the PLO as a representative of the Palestinians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But soon, fierce political rivalry between Hamas and Fatah occurred.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, it was not just a matter of elections and "you win" and "I win"; it was actually civil war, violence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The rise of the radical hard-right extremists in both societies, in fact, have made a peaceful political settlement almost impossible.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We sit here or stand here and talk about a two-state solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And actually support for a two-state negotiated political solution has been dropping, waning in both those societies.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, in a very perverse way, the extremist right-wing in both Israel and amongst the Palestinians believe in a "one-state solution".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But if you think about it, a one-state solution, by definition, means the violent elimination of the other.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am making the point this is difficult, this is complicated and we should respect that difficulty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Nevertheless, it is our sincere hope that, over time, both sides will muster the political will.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, I should digress, they need the political leadership with the conviction, the courage and the political capital, which they are willing to expend in order to make a two-state solution a reality.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if they do not, then they are doomed to repeat the cycles of violence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have regular high-level exchanges and visits with the Palestinian Authority, which have allowed us to meet them, hear them and discuss issues with them candidly.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My sixth point is that we must not allow external political events, painful as they are, to divide us in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Yesterday, the Prime Minister reminded us this is not our quarrel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a quarrel amongst our friends outside.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our job is to be sympathetic, compassionate, to speak truth to them, to be helpful, but not to pour oil on the fire.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And bear in mind, actually, both sides claim to be the children of Abraham.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is the ultimate example of sibling fratricide.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both sides have suffered tragic losses and they deserve our sympathy and support.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But come back now to Singapore and be very wary and careful in how we reflect our compassion, our principles, our values.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Understand that strong emotions are engaged, but we must not fall prey to what we see in other countries where strong emotions have led to violent clashes, to hate speech and to exclusion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as many of you have illustrated, often fueled by disinformation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our religious and racial harmony is very precious.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must not allow anything to break this or split our society.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And it is heartening that so many of our faith and community leaders strongly feel this, say this and operate on this basis.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Mufti, Dr Nazirudin Nasir wrote a letter, which I hope every single one of you will read, to express solidarity and support to the Rabbi Mordechai Abergel, who replied in the same spirit.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It was an exemplary gesture of goodwill that reflects so well on our religious harmony.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But it is actually quite rare in the world for a Mufti and a Rabbi to be able to correspond like that at a moment of tension and high emotion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I can assure you, the Government had nothing to do with this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we saw it and approved of it and we should all be grateful to them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At its core, the conflict has always been about territory, self-determination and identity, complicated by intra-Palestinian and intra-Israeli domestic politics.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as I have said before, it provides fertile ground for extremists on both sides to misuse religion to further their political aims and we must not fall into their trap.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The seventh point is that the safety of Singaporeans abroad is always a priority for us in MFA.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do our best to remain in contact with them; they have chosen to remain.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As human beings, we cannot remain detached and inured to human suffering, but we know these cycles of violence will recur unless they come to the nub of the problem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As Singaporeans, we do care and we do care deeply, but this episode is also a reminder to all Singaporeans that we do have our national interests at stake.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must reject terrorism in all its forms.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: No excuses, no ifs, no buts, no short-term political advantage.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If attacked, all of us here must give the government of the day the ability to exercise the right of self-defence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But even when it does so, we will expect the government of the day to uphold international law.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As Singaporeans, we will continue to extend humanitarian assistance and protection to all civilians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should support the peaceful resolution of disputes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must nurture and protect our own precious cohesion and harmony.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must never allow conflicts elsewhere to divide us domestically.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am glad that today that my sense of the House is that we have unanimity, we will have consensus in voting for this Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think, the Minister, correct me if I am wrong, the Minister was, for lack of a better word, curious why the words "terrorist attack" were not in our statement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I thought that would have made it clear that we were taking a very even-keeled approach to this matter, that on the one hand, the terrorist attacks are not to be condoned; on the other hand, when you have matters such as Israeli settlers evicting Palestinians from their homes in the West Bank – even today, it is happening today – that also ought to be condemned.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I hope the Minister can agree that there has to be an even-handed approach to this.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My second point, perhaps explaining why the use of that word "terrorism" was not activated so readily but more of a balanced approach in our statement was what we sought to put forward – is with regard to Singapore's approach on the labelling of organisations or terrorist designations on certain groups.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I understand Singapore has an Inter-Ministry Committee on Terrorist Designation (IMC-TD).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is the authority of the designation of terrorist groups and groupings.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Government relies on this committee to determine which organisation is labelled accordingly and then this is legislatively captured in the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act 2002.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Maybe the Minister can explain that position for the understanding of the general public.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My final point relates to something which was originally said by Mr Alex Yam.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Minister also made the same point by way of the document that has been released to Members, where he said that Singapore has been consistent in its stand on matters concerning Israel and Palestine.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I had a quick look at statements that were made by Mr Lee Kuan Yew over the years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I also noted what he said in his memoirs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He spoke of the Six-Day War and I am quoting from his memoirs, "When the UN General Assembly was debating the resolution to condemn Israel, Rajaratnam, our Foreign Minister and Afro-Asian champion, was all for it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Keng Swee saw me to press Raja to direct our UN delegate not to avoid in favour of the resolution or the Israelis would leave." By "the Israelis would leave", he is referring to the Israeli advisors who were here in assisting the build-up of the Singapore Armed Forces.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Thereafter, Mr Lee said, "As I could not attend the Cabinet meeting, I stated my position in a note.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We had to stand up for the right of small nations to exist." And he goes on, "I added that I did not believe the Israeli advisors would leave even if we were to vote for the Afro-Asian resolution.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It may well be that the resolution Mr Lee is referring to is a different one, but I am just making that point to clarify what the Minister has put out in his statement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I just want to, I suppose, double confirm on the actions that Hamas conducted on 7 October targeting innocent civilians at home, killing women, children and taking hostages – is the WP's position that those are acts of terrorism?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is why I said I was more reassured, Mr Speaker, after listening to both of them, because the initial statement did leave some room for doubt and ambiguity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My conclusion from this recent confirmation is that actually, you stand four-square with us, with the Motion and with the Government's position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I want to welcome that because, again, the arguments on foreign policy must stop at our shores.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And on something as vital as terrorism, we cannot afford to have political parties trying to outflank each other in order to fish for votes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am grateful for the WP's confirmation that you stand on this issue, that what happened on that day was a terrorist act, deserves unequivocal condemnation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I think PSP has also made its position clear.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second line of queries about terrorists' designation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Generally, different countries have different ways of designating.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The United States and the European Union (EU) have their list of terrorist organisations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The UN generally works on the basis of what is designated by the Security Council.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What we are looking out for are acts of terrorism, financing of terrorism.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Whether someone or some organisation is or is not on a list in the UN or some other country is just one factor under consideration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is that old saying, "If it walks like a duck, it quacks like a duck, it is a duck." I think I have to ask you to trust our security agencies that they know what activities and plans people are up to and where that money is going to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not a binary switch – you are on the list or you are not on the list.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You notice that I have been also very careful to say what I am asking you to confirm today is that the actions of 7 October were acts of terror.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you want to go further back in history, I have made the point earlier that yes, it is not a secret that we do have a good relationship with Israel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But a good relationship does not mean we have to agree with everything they do nor are we apologists for what they do.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is worth remembering, to come back to Gaza, that in fact 18 years ago, Israel had to deploy its own military forces in Gaza to force its settlers out of Gaza, 18 years ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I said just now, Maliki and myself have been to Ramallah a couple of times.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They know why we take the stand we take.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The larger point I want to make to Members of this Houses is that it is why it is so important to operate by principles and to consistently operate by principles.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because from time to time, whoever is on this side of the House will have to say "no". "No" to a superpower, "no" to a friend who has been there at a time when we were very vulnerable and needed help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But without that sense of principle and that consistent adherence to principle, we will make life much more difficult for our country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the conduct of foreign policy, like I said, will become a very much more dangerous enterprise than it is now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Frankly, for this matter, the foreign policy aspects of it are not difficult.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The real challenge – the real political challenge – is domestic.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why I have been so keen and listening for the support from Members of Parliament of all parties and from the Nominated Members of Parliament as well for this Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I just wanted to get a sense from the Minister as I put in my original set of clarifications, how would he characterise what happened in the occupied territories?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think that is important for a more balanced perspective to this issue.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I think it is important that the Government sets its view out as well.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think I stated it just now and I would put out our voting record at the UN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You do not need to ask me for that.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, if Hamas is not on the list, it does not mean that it is not a terrorist entity.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: There are other limbs but these three are the most material.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: If that is satisfied, in addition to that, where the threat or use of violence is reasonably regarded or intending to influence or compel government or any other government or any international organisations to do or refrain from doing any act or intimidate the public or public servant or the public, then it is an act of terrorism.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, to me, all the components are satisfied.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Before he put his view out, he said that our statement did not condemn it because of this particular point, or because of terrorism.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In our view, at the time the statement was made, a condemnation of both parties was important to us, for different reasons, of course.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And so, we captured it in the fourth paragraph of our statement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, like many Singaporeans, I am deeply troubled and saddened by the loss of civilian lives on all sides and the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Starting with the shocking attack that took the lives of 1,400 ordinary Israelis, now on a daily basis, we see images of devastation and despair; of the innocent lives lost, including more than 3,700 Palestinian children in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is heartbreaking to think about the children who were orphaned because they lost their parents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Understandably, our Muslim community particularly, feel anxious, restless, sad and even angry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This humanitarian crisis facing the Palestinian people is a truly heartbreaking tragedy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Government understands the emotions felt and expressed by our Muslim community and other Singaporeans towards the plight of Palestinians in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The daily rising death toll is of grave concern.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We deeply sympathise with the plight and the grief of Palestinian civilians who have lost their loved ones, just as we feel deep sympathy for the grieving families of Israelis killed in the 7 October attacks, although the death toll in Palestine has increased multiple folds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We convey our deepest condolences to the families of all civilians killed and wounded in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, we need to also understand the present crisis in the context of history.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The conflict goes back a long way and is highly complicated.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this case, Hamas' terrorist attacks on 7 October, which massacred many Israeli civilians.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have now called for the unconditional, safe and immediate release of all civilians held hostage in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Israel has the legitimate right within international law to defend its citizens and territory from armed attacks and acts of terror, just like Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But it has to do so in accordance with international humanitarian law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is the same acts of terror we cannot allow on anyone and more so on our shores.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I have spoken to many Palestinians and their leaders there.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have not been able to live the peace – the same one Singaporeans cherish - for a very long time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore believes in and complies with the rule of law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That lasting peace that Palestine desires must undergo the process of law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian had shared our voting records in the UN on the Palestinian issue from as early as 1967 when Israel occupied Palestine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And most recently, at the resumed 10th UN General Assembly (UNGA) Emergency Special Session on 27 October, Singapore voted for a UNGA resolution which demanded that all parties comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and to enable immediate and sustained humanitarian access for essential supplies and services to reach all civilians in need in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The resolution also calls for the immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce, leading to cessation of hostilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some Members have asked about Singapore's response towards humanitarian aid to Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is the single largest contribution that the Governmen has made to support humanitarian and relief efforts in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will consider giving more as the need arises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans have largely been careful to not let what is happening overseas affect our social harmony at home, even though our heart goes out to those affected in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We appreciate both the Muslim and Jewish communities here acting with calm and exercising restraint.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Religious leaders like the Mufti and Chief Rabbi expressed sympathy, provided reassurances and gave support to each other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This reflects that our model of co-existence is possible, and as one people, we must do all we can to preserve such social harmony that we have built in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Seeing the alternative model in the Middle East today, we cannot take for granted what we have achieved today and we must continue to work hard to preserve it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened to see that Singaporeans readily stepped forward to contribute generously to the humanitarian relief efforts in various ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are touched by the generous donations received thus far, which have been heartening, but more importantly, we see Singaporeans' strong spirit of solidarity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many different community and interfaith groups came together to contribute to RLAF's humanitarian aid and to Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Members may also access the handout through the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will receive a briefing from these humanitarian organizations on the latest humanitarian situation in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And I will also take the opportunity to meet and discuss with the Egyptian leaders about opportunities for us to collaborate to help the victims in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some Members have also asked about Singapore's relations with the Palestinian Authority (PA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have recognized the right of Israel to exist and pursue the 2-state solutions that we have supported and we have voted for at the UN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have engaged the PA leadership at the highest level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since early 2022, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, Minister Vivian and I have visited Ramallah.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We welcome PA officials to make study visits to Singapore and participate in courses under the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also hope for more PA officials to take up available scholarships to pursue their postgraduate studies at Singapore's universities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Singapore Representative Office in Ramallah continues to operate and will support ETAP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, true peace and reconciliation can only occur when both Israeli and Palestinian people commit to a two-state solution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For that to happen, both Israel and the Palestinians need the political will to make the compromises necessary to resolve the conflict that they have been facing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Their people will decide on their respective leaders who, in turn, will decide if and when they can ensure peace will prevail.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It should not and must not happen due to pressure from the social media war.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Least so by violence, even when it is to avenge violence – that can never be the answer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It will only harden hearts for another generation and make any resolution even more difficult.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Difficult as it may be given the current conflict in Gaza, we hope that there will be a time in the future for both sides to enter direct negotiations on the basis of a two-state solution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The perpetual cycle of violence must be broken.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a friend to both Israel and the Palestinians, it is Singapore's sincere hope that peace will ultimately prevail.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, please allow me to continue my speech in English.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some Members have asked about the impact of the Israeli-Hamas conflict on Singapore society and the efforts taken to strengthen our religious harmony, including in our educational institutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As mentioned in my Malay speech earlier, we recognise that the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is an emotive one for Singaporeans and there may be different viewpoints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Regardless, the peace and harmony that we enjoy in Singapore are precious and many in the House have spoken about this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have worked hard over the years to build up trust across our different communities at different levels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We all have a duty of care to protect and grow it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the leadership level, we have multiple platforms for community leaders to engage with one another frequently and at different settings, such as at the National Steering Committee on Racial and Religious Harmony, as well as the Racial and Religious Harmony Circles in every constituency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the people-to-people level, MCCY provides support for inter-faith and inter-ethnic dialogues and other initiatives that bring together different communities to respectfully discuss sensitive issues of race and religion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example: Ask Me Anything: a series of dialogues that educates the public about different faiths in Singapore and seeks to develop inter-faith norms and practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: OnePeople.SG organises Community Dialogues in collaboration with community groups that engage a broad spectrum of participants in robust yet respectful conversations on sensitive issues of race and religion and on social norms and aspirations of the different communities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Within the Muslim community, religious leaders and asatizahs play an important role to guide and support the community during this difficult period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They amplified values of Rahmah, or blessings, and called upon the community to embrace compassion, blessings and love for all.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is in line with the principles and values of Islam as "Blessings for All".

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Mufti has engaged youths at a MuslimSG event on 14 October and provided guidance on how, as Muslims, we should respond and deal with our feelings of grief and anger, which must be guided by the teachings of Islam and being a blessing to all.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) has also produced a series of Friday sermons that speaks on the need to preserve peace and compassion and the sanctity of human lives, regardless of one's religion and background.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our asatizahs also bring the community together to pray for peace and the cessation of violence, not only in Gaza, but elsewhere.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These special prayers not only provide solace for the community to respond to the situation but empower them to pray for peace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must continue to protect ourselves from being influenced by the barrage of information, misinformation and disinformation that enters our social media platforms as feeds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we engage students in understanding global issues, such as the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, we will continue to emphasise Singapore's multicultural context and the importance of preserving our precious racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students are reminded to be respectful and constructive during these discussions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some may have personal connections to the developing situation in the Middle East.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We ought to be mindful and take extra effort to be respectful, sensitive and kind and appreciate their feelings and experiences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, let us not let these perspectives hurt our relationships and unity in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am proud of how Singaporeans are responding to the situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It shows a recognition that we should not let external developments divide Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Let us continue to work together to build up the bonds of trust and harmony in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I wish you safe travels to Egypt tonight, Dr Maliki Osman.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.25 pm until 4.45 pm.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As Singaporeans, we have a duty to support our country's stance, expressed here in Parliament today.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singaporeans and residents must remain united to uphold our domestic peace, harmony and mutual respect.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I want to acknowledge the emotions and reactions of all our fellow Singaporeans, which can be very diverse, with some experiencing stronger emotions than others.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am sure that everyone experiences, to varying degrees, the distress and heartache of learning about fellow human lives being lost.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As Singaporeans, we treasure a peaceful world, with many of our older generations still holding memories of the trauma of war and the immense amount of blood, sweat and tears required to rebuild a nation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is with this shared history and destiny that bind all of us, past, present and future Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In today's modern warfare that is globally televised, and with social media playing a pivotal role in shaping the world's perceptions of the situation, misinformation and disinformation from supporters of all sides will certainly take place.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It has happened and will continue to happen.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Social media content, in its nature, is designed to rile people up, sustain their interest and become viral.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just like how all of us are learning how to deal with scammers, we must also learn how to resist being influenced and blindly led along by social media in this conflict.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must not play into their hands and we must not let ourselves get dragged into the conflict virtually.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Beyond the virtual online world, what about in the real world?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I want to take this opportunity to talk about the safety and security of Singaporeans who are overseas when emergencies, conflicts or crises strike.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: When the situations in Ukraine and in Israel deteriorated or when borders were closed and flights were cancelled at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, there were Singaporeans who were on their travels.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many Singaporeans travel overseas, be it to neighbouring countries within Southeast Asia or other destinations further away.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we get more Singaporeans to eRegister before leaving?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While many of my residents told me that they do eRegister before leaving, there are still many who shared me with that they had forgotten to do so on quite a number of trips or felt it was not necessary.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I suggest this be a voluntary step to be built into existing immigration and customs processes or more reminders can be put up prominently via QR codes at the airports or border crossings.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I make this speech with a heavy heart, not from a weight of reluctance or hesitation, but from a place of deep anguish and pain.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The conflict is a tragedy unfolding so catastrophically that in barely over a month, more than 10,000 lives have been lost.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We see troubling and abhorrent images on both sides; on 7 October from within Israel and then, over the past month, from Gaza.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We have yet to consider, Mr Deputy Speaker, the longer-term impact of food security, water and sanitation, health and healthcare, destruction to family units, the impact of education of children and the physical infrastructure damage to housing units, education facilities, hospitals and other buildings are also included in the UN report.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: These numbers inform us of a humanitarian crisis and tragedy so deep, protracted and entrenched that it will take years, if not decades, to recover from.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I am hopeful for peace and a two-state solution in my lifetime, but certainly, no peace can be had when guns, rockets and airstrikes are still firing from both sides and countless innocent civilians are losing lives on a daily basis.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Taking a leaf from the statement by our Ambassador Burhan Gafoor, our Permanent Representative at the Emergency Special Session of the United Nations General Assembly, on 27 October 2023, I quote: "We support the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland and Israel's right to live within secure borders.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Both Palestinians and Israelis deserve to live in peace, security and dignity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We call on leaders from both sides to show leadership, to exercise restraint and to take the difficult but necessary steps towards the vision of a two-state solution." Mr Deputy Speaker, I have two proposals for the Government to further consider as part of my contribution to this debate and Motion.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It speaks to what both our hon Foreign Ministers have said earlier.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The first takes into account that Singapore is no stranger to difficult conversations, conflict resolution and negotiations.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our stated positions across many conflicting issues on the international stage have been clear and principled, even if it may bring some detriment, disagreement or unhappiness in our relationships with other countries in the short term.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The position of trust and honesty at the international stage that Singapore has benefited from could only have been possible because we continue to take consistent principled positions in our dealings and affairs with others and anchored firmly in our prescribed values of justice and equality for all.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I would urge the Government to build on the trusted partnership that Singapore has on both sides of the fence of this conflict and take a position of arbitration, if and when the opportunity arises, publicly or otherwise.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Depending on how one measures the timeline of this conflict, surely, there are differing historical views and narratives on when this conflict started.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, my view is that learning from history has its benefits and we surely must be introspective about such lessons but only in so far as it does not hold us ransom and hinder current and future prospects of peace.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore has shown through examples of her actions internally in our local context and outwardly on the international stage that we have no qualms about proposing and making considered decisions based on what is right rather than what is popular.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Being a small country in the global space with little by way of physical resources, our value has been measured through the trust that others have in us.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Further to this, our local communities also have an innumerable number of scholars who are familiar with the wider Middle East, its language, culture and history and these are strengths that we can draw upon to facilitate such an involvement in the peace process.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, there is much that the wider Singapore society and the Government can learn and glean from this conflict.
