speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: These range from wider issues of international relations relating to foreign diplomacy, deterrence and defence, to internal lessons about how fragile society can be when societal differences are amplified along racial and religious ideologies coupled with a lack political will, stability and ability to achieve peaceful resolution in the longer term.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Inadvertently, the ones who suffer most as a result are innocent civilians and the people.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There should be means for Singapore Citizens to discuss and express their thoughts in a safe space about such delicate issues and raise their own awareness and appreciation of such devastation and atrocities happening around the world.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Where there are additional concerns relating to security or public order, such engagements could be done with certain security restrictions or in limited numbers of participants.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We should continue to allow for peaceful discussion of such issues so that people with polarising views can discuss such matters respectfully and sensitively.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As a Singaporean, I also take heed that what we have here in Singapore; living amongst groups of variable religious persuasions and racial identities, yet still remaining united as one people, is something we should never take for granted.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is something we should guard fiercely and recognise that in another part of the world, this still remains a very distant possibility at best.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In my speech, I wish to focus on the response of our Singapore Muslim community, particularly our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Across the world, we have seen, troublingly, a deepening divide across religious lines spilling, on many occasions, into overt hate crimes as a response.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the US, a landlord was charged with murder and hate crime for killing a 6-year-old Muslim boy and seriously wounding his mother in Illinois.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The landlord allegedly did so because of their religion and the conflict between Hamas and Israel.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There were numerous reports from US-based news agencies pointing to worsening Islamophobia leading to hate-fueled attacks and other discriminatory incidents in the country.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: At the same time, antisemitism was also reported to be on the rise across the world.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For instance, just on 3 November 2023, the UK Guardian reported that Jewish people in Britain experienced the worst wave of hate incidents in modern times with more than 1,000 recorded to date.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the US, Reuters reported that antisemitic incidents rose by about 400% in two weeks since the Hamas led attack in Israel.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have also seen demonstrations in many major cities where anger is being openly stoked with very divisive messages.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The narrative is often styled on an "us versus them" basis.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A number of organisations have propagated violence at the demonstrations, which will inevitably lead to even more polarization along racial, religious and also nationality lines.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The right of civilians to live peacefully must be protected at all times".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He further noted that both Islam and Jewish scriptures emphasised the human need for mercy and compassion.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Unlike so many others outside Singapore, the Mufti separated the violent acts of humans from the religions of Islam and Judaism.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is worth emphasising in times like this when lines are drawn precisely along religious lines.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Mufti deplored the violence and deaths arising from both the terrorists acts of Hamas as well as from Israeli military operations.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I particularly felt the calling out against terrorist acts of Hamas was important for a diverse, multiracial and religious country like Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As was mentioned numerous times by our Government leaders, Singapore is not immune to a terrorist attack.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Should a terrorist attack happen here and hostages are taken, we would expect Singapore to retaliate in self defence, in accordance with public international law too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On the point of retaliation in self defence, the requirements under international law are clear.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Unfortunately, in conflicts, the total avoidance of civilian casualty is impossible.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, there are principles such as necessity, not targeting civilians, proportionality and avoiding unnecessary suffering which, when applied, will have the effect of reducing such casualty.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also understand from my Muslim friends that Mufti's message was reinforced during Friday sermons and delivered by the imams at our mosques.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In these sermons, a call was made to pray for world peace in these troubled times and to advocate "goodwill and peace".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have spoken to a good number of my Muslim community leaders, friends and residents in Bukit Batok on Mufti's message.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Without exception, the Mufti's message resonated strongly with them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Each of them told me that, personally, they are deeply affected by the humanitarian crisis.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The numerous videos and news articles that they have received from social media platforms conveying the brutal tragedy of the war have affected their conscience.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If ever there is a silver lining to this tragedy, they noted the renewed discussion within the international community on the two-state solution which is now increasingly seen as a necessity and bulwark against perpetuation of further violence in future.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We should recognise, with the developments across the world, particularly amongst Muslim countries, this is not an easy position for our Muslim Singaporeans to take.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In 1965, when Singapore was founded, our founding father and 1st Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, exhorted all racial communities, including our Malay community, to build a Singapore for all Singaporeans from all races.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My sincere thanks to our Malay and Muslim communities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These are the clarifications following on some of the questions which the Leader of the Opposition had asked just now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will not hesitate to take firm action against any individual or entity that poses a security threat, including barring entry into Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I refer all of you to the Terrorism Suppression of Financing Act of 2002, both section 2 as well as the Second Schedule.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the point is, it depends on the actions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I thought that is an important clarification which I shall leave on the table.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would be happy to send the list to the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other point was his question about the resolutions which happened in 1967.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I told the House we voted in favour of five resolutions which were passed, primarily to do with humanitarian assistance and the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There was one other resolution that we abstained on, but in the end, it was not carried because it did not have a sufficient majority.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And this was a resolution that the then-Non-Aligned Movement was trying to pass on 3 July, calling, amongst other things, for the immediate withdrawal of some military forces – but you must understand, in the immediate aftermath of a war, that would have been controversial.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Anyway, we abstained but that resolution was not carried, in any case.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the first clarification, I take the Minister's point.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My simple rejoinder earlier was that Hamas was not on that list.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I was not questioning whether the Act did not capture them or anything of that sort.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If you look at the list, it appears to be a positive list.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the second point, I note the Minister's clarification.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Surely, you are not saying you did not call them out because it was not on the list?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But anyway, let us not get bogged down there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The point is, today, in this House, you have agreed, we have all agreed, the acts that were conducted on 7 October were acts of terrorism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The international community is urgently trying to manage the situation – to expand and sustain the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza and to minimise further loss of civilian lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our Muslim community in Singapore feel it more strongly because of the empathy and compassion for the Palestinian cause, but no matter our race, our religion or our background, all of us cannot help but grieve that so many lives have been lost and many more remain in danger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we try to make sense of what is happening, we must recognise that what we are seeing did not erupt overnight.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As many have already explained, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is a deeply complex one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a long-standing feud going back at least decades, if not centuries, involving multiple state and non-state actors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The conflict is not just between Israelis and Palestinians or between people of different faiths, as Minister Vivian had explained just now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a political battle for territory, self determination and identity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is at stake, also, is the broader balance of power in the Middle East.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Throughout history, this land corridor between the Mediterranean coast and the vast Arabian desert has been the battleground of ancient kingdoms and civilisations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You go back to the Egyptians, Babylonians and Romans to the Ottomans, the British and the French.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That battle for regional influence continues today, including between Iran and its Arab neighbours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For years, Iran has been funding, training and arming Hamas as well as other militia in the region, including Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is certainly no coincidence that the brutal attacks by Hamas happened just after Israel normalised relations with the UAE and was in negotiations to do so with Saudi Arabia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hamas must have anticipated a strong Israeli response when it launched its attacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, it may well have counted on this so as to rally people in the Middle East to its cause.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But any country facing such attacks must respond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, it is distressing to see the military response by Israel now taking such a terrible toll on civilians in Gaza.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The issue threatens to spill over into a much larger regional conflict with major global implications.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the end, after all this, who are the victims?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The victims are the Palestinian people themselves, who are being used as pawns and human shields amidst this proxy fight amongst bigger and regional powers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this is a stark reminder to everyone in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We live in a dangerous world with complex geopolitics everywhere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not import foreign quarrels or politics here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we always choose what is in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Both Ministers Vivian and Maliki have both laid out at length Singapore's position on this matter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will not revisit everything they have said, but let me emphasise two important points that bear repeating.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hamas has said they are ready to repeat these heinous attacks to "bring about the annihilation of Israel".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Palestinian people have many historical grievances which we empathise with.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there can be no excuse, no justification whatsoever, for the wanton acts of violence and terrorism by Hamas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is in our national interest to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To compromise on this stand would be to compromise our own security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This right to defend one's citizens and territory is a fundamental right enshrined in the UN Charter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this case, it means Israel has the right to take action to prevent Hamas from attacking again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in exercising this right, Israel must comply fully with the letter and spirit of international humanitarian law and the rules governing the conduct of war.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under the Geneva Conventions, it must respond in a proportionate manner and do its utmost to protect the security and safety of civilians.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, no matter how gruesome the acts of terrorism committed by Hamas, they cannot justify a disproportionate response by Israel that imposes collective punishment on the Palestinians in Gaza.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If Israel violates international humanitarian law, it risks losing the moral high ground and undermining its own cause both domestically and internationally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The discussions around these international rules can be fraught and subject to differing views and perspectives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But from a humanitarian point of view, the catastrophe now happening in Gaza is horrific and unbearable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also urge Israel to facilitate the supply of food, water, medical supplies and fuel in Gaza.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will do our part to assist in global relief efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am glad that many Singaporeans have responded to the calls for assistance, including by donating generously to the fundraising appeals by the Singapore Red Cross and Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are concrete and practical things we can all do in Singapore in response to this human tragedy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We believe that the Palestinian people have the right to a homeland and that Israel has the right to live within secure borders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Realising this may seem difficult, now more than ever, but that should not deter us from continuing to support the international community's efforts in this area.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Both the Palestinians and Israelis know our position and our principles well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have good relations with the Palestinians and have committed substantial technical assistance and support to the Palestinian Authority over the years and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have a strong, long-standing relationship with Israel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Israel helped build up the SAF during our early years and we continue to cooperate closely with them across many areas, including in science and technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are friends with both Israel and the Palestinians.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it does not mean we support everything each side does.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we consistently take a principled position, in line with international law and in support of global peace and security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On that basis, we have voted in favour of many Palestinian-related resolutions at the UN over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have criticised Israel's settlement activities in the West Bank as violations of international law.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also voted against Jerusalem being recognised as the capital of Israel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, such unilateral moves by Israel detract from the two-state solution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is partly the reason why more and more Palestinians feel that violence is the only way to achieve their goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The international community must therefore give Palestinians reasons to think otherwise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A non-violent path to an independent Palestinian state must be made unmistakably clear.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then the ideas of organisations like Hamas and its belief in the use of violence and terrorism can truly be defeated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In all that we do, Sir, Singapore will act in accordance with our national interest and we will consistently choose principles and international law.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is what makes a small nation like us a credible, reliable and trusted partner on the international stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond upholding our national interests, we must not allow external events like these to divide us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because in such conflicts, individual passions are bound to be aroused.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this age of social media, images, videos and stories will be frequently propagated online specifically to rile up emotions and sow distrust.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This can turn a faraway conflict into an emotionally charged issue that can easily spiral out of control, even here in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have already seen instances of hate speech and religiously motivated attacks elsewhere in recent days.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In France, a teacher was fatally stabbed by a Russian-Muslim attacker amid rising tensions between the Jewish and Muslim communities there.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the US, a six-year-old Palestinian-American was fatally stabbed and his mother wounded by an American in a religiously motivated hate crime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore is not immune to such divisive forces.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have worked so hard over the years to foster social harmony across our different communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have built up networks of friendship and trust across different community and religious leaders through platforms like the Racial and Religious Harmony Circles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We regularly promote inter-faith and inter-ethnic dialogue to bring together different communities and to respectfully discuss sensitive issues of race and religion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our schools and IHLs are also involved to teach our young to interact with one another in a safe and respectful way, and to help them to understand global issues in the context of Singapore's unique multicultural milieu.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I am very glad that our community and religious leaders understand what is at stake.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our religious leaders, in particular, are expressing their views in a way that shows sensitivity, compassion and kindness; so as not to destabilise peace and harmony in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have led many positive efforts to emphasise unity, not division.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When the conflict first erupted, as all of you know, Mufti Ustaz Dr Nazirudin Mohd Nasir wrote to the Chief Rabbi Mordechai Abergel in Singapore, who later replied to him, and both expressed empathy and solidarity with one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Inter-Religious Organisation brought together various faith leaders to pray for peace and the safety of civilians in both Israel and Gaza.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On such emotive issues, it makes all the difference to have religious leaders who understand what is happening and what is at stake for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are able to guide their flock and help to hold the social cohesion and trust between our different religious groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some may think that this guidance is not necessary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The more extreme religious leaders on all sides also tend to be the ones who are more emotional, more vocal in pressing their case, in advocating their own narratives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those calling for peace, dialogue and engagement tend to be the ones who are drowned out or silenced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The end result is not more light but more darkness, not more peace and harmony but more division and hatred in society and we certainly do not want that to happen in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we should be very, very grateful for the leadership shown by our religious leaders like Mufti and Chief Rabbi.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us, as individuals, can all do our part too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will continue to provide safe spaces for such sensitive conversations to take place, but we should do our part to be respectful and constructive in our dialogue and discourse, both online and offline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We should strive to listen to and empathise with one another, especially when we disagree and have different views and we should not hesitate to call loud inflammatory language which seek to turn communities against each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this way, we can collectively strengthen the peace and social cohesion that is essential to the Singaporean way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am glad that all Members of the House are with the Government on this, as we have heard in all the speeches so far.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The WP and the PSP have put out their Parties' position on this matter and, indeed, their positions are consistent with the Government's position, indeed, the national position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We were a little concerned at first with the WP's statement for the reasons highlighted – because it stopped short of condemning Hamas; it referred to it as a "military operation" rather than a terrorist act.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Leader of the Opposition, Mr Singh, has explained the context and the circumstances behind the WP's statement, so we understand, but I am sure Mr Singh would also appreciate, without the benefit of his explanation earlier, there was ambiguity about that statement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There were questions raised about the WP's stance on the actions of Hamas and some might even ask whether the WP had deliberately overlooked this just to appear more sympathetic to the Palestinian cause.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I am very glad that Mr Singh has stood up and explained the WP's position clearly and has condemned Hamas' acts as acts of terrorism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, perhaps, if he is so minded, Mr Singh might update the WP's social media platform to reflect this position so that there is no ambiguity about the matter whatsoever.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a key point of principle because national security is at stake.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, Sir, indeed, in situations like this, we must stand united.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Politics must stop at the water's edge and that means on external matters where national security is at stake, political parties should not try to outflank the Government just to score political points.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us not risk our precious unity for short-term political gain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not when our collective security and fundamental interests are at stake.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us owe this basic duty to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the end of this debate, I hope all of us, everyone in this House – PAP, WP, PSP as well as all Nominated Members – wilI support the Motion and we can have a common pro-Singapore's stand on the matter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members also asked about the economic and security implications of the conflict on Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the security front, Singapore can draw lessons from what has happened.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The surprise attack by Hamas caught Israel off guard.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a potent reminder that we must always be vigilant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why, since 9/11, we have raised our defence capabilities to respond to terror attacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, through the Counter-Terrorism Information Facility, we work closely with other countries to share intelligence and to provide early warning against terrorism in the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The SAF and the Home Team conduct regular exercises, and these have also helped to raise a high level of readiness in our society against terror attacks, be it from air, land or sea.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the ongoing conflict, these efforts have certainly gained greater salience because we know that Singapore is an attractive target for foreign terrorist groups as well as self-radicalised individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And while Israel and Gaza may be far away, what happens in the Middle East can affect us here in Southeast Asia and Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We fully expect extremist and terrorist groups in the region to use this conflict to rile up sentiments and radicalise more individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, amidst this conflict, it is more urgent than ever that we prepare for all contingencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why our security agencies are on heightened alert, and we have put in place additional security measures as a precaution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us, Singaporeans, must stay vigilant too, by reporting any suspicious behaviour or activity to the authorities because in the end, our ability to respond to any terrorist incident depends on all of us as Singaporeans working together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must remain cohesive and united as a society, so that we can keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That, above all else, we are more similar than we are different.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That we can rise above what divides us, and embrace our shared humanity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I spoke earlier about the exchange of letters between Mufti and the Chief Rabbi of Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore has gone through much to get to where we are today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans of all races and religions can live side by side.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just two points for the Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Number one, he spoke of a request for us to update the WP's statement of the 18 October.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, we will append our speeches to that statement and it should make our position quite clear.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On 18 of October, I did not get any message from the Minister for Foreign Affairs or anyone, suggesting to me that our statement was problematic from a national security angle.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I would like to assure the Foreign Minister and, of course, the Government as well and the Deputy Prime Minister, that in future, if the Government has an inkling of such a concern, that there are national security matters or issues which the opposition may not be apprised of or we may have completely ignored, let us know.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My assurance to the Deputy Prime Minister is that we will certainly take those views on board very carefully – because as the Deputy Prime Minister mentioned, at the end of the day, we want a Singapore where we have a united population even though we know that the issue tugs at the heart strings of people on both sides.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, that is my assurance to the Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And then we are all in a common position on that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But united as Singaporeans, we can overcome all challenges together.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: First, it reiterates Singapore's principled approach to such conflicts and our commitment to UN's processes and rule of international law as underlying basis for international relations.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This has been our consistent approach and it is an important foreign policy cornerstone for us as a small state.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Third, the Motion calls on us in Singapore to uphold and protect our multiracial and multi-religious way of life.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We have seen how this conflict has precipitated racial attacks in several countries.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Guardian reported yesterday that Britain is facing the worst wave of hate incidents in modern times, with 1,000 recorded after the Hamas attack, which included assaults targeting children and schools.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore, our strong multi-religious and multiracial relations act as a bulwark against such reactions, aside, of course, from such acts being illegal and liable to strict prosecution by the authorities.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: While inter-community trust in Singapore is high, dialogue among the Government, religious leaders and Singaporeans of all communities is critical to keep our peace and I understand that significant efforts have been made in this regard.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is important for us to continue to do so, and everyone has a part to play, as mentioned by other speakers.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The current conflict is not a new conflict.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is an escalation of sustained attacks by Hamas on Israel over more than two decades and responses by Israel.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Since 2001, Palestinian militants have launched tens of thousands of rocket and motor attacks on Israel from the Gaza Strip.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These attacks have been described and condemned as terrorist attacks by the United Nations.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These attacks have also been condemned by the Palestinian Authority that governs the West Bank, as it says that rocket attacks undermine peace.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In 2023, before October, there were over 1,500 sporadic rocket attacks into Israel, with the largest attack in May 2013.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Israel's Foreign Minister told the United Nations, following the October attack, that Israel had vowed to destroy Hamas.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: He said and I quote, "How can you agree to a ceasefire with someone who swore to kill and destroy your own existence?" But, Sir, the situation is complex.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Both Jews and Arabs claim a historical right to territories in and surrounding Israel.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Layered on this are overlapping religious claims and sensitivities.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Al-Aqsa Mosque, which sits atop the Temple Mount and Wailing Wall, for example, continues to be a recurring flashpoint.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I led a trade delegation to Israel in May this year.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We arrived the week after a barrage of rocket launches into Israel.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Israelis have built for themselves a modern cosmopolitan country in which they enjoy a First-World lifestyle despite the constant threat of attacks.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I extended my stay after the trade trip and made my way into Bethlehem and Hebron in the West Bank.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The West Bank is markedly different from neighbouring Israel, with a significantly lower quality of life.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I went past checkpoints and saw from afar the Jewish settlements and security surrounding it.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: On the one hand, I understood the Israeli security measures.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: On the other, I understood the Palestinians' desire for freedom of movement in their own land.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I could also see that there was no easy solution.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: One thing that is clear, however, is that both the Israeli and Palestinian peoples' overriding desire is self-determination.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The right to decide their own destiny and the right to live in their country with security and freedom of movement with access to economic amenities and jobs and opportunities for advancement.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that Singaporeans will see the complexity of the situation in the Middle East.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not so easy to unequivocally say "I support Israel" or "I support the Palestinians", because there are legitimate justifications, arguments and concerns on both sides.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, Ambassador Burhan Gafoor's qualifications in his explanation on our vote in the United Nations on the protection of civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations is as important as Singapore's vote in favour of the resolution.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Ambassador Gafoor deeply regretted, first, that the resolution omitted to mention Hamas' abhorrent attack on Israel and the abduction of innocent hostages; and, second, that it also omitted to acknowledge Israel's legitimate right to defend its citizens and territory.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But armed conflicts invariably lead to tragedy, as people lose their lives, their loved ones and their homes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: What we can see definitively is that we support humanity and the alleviation of the suffering of people who are caught in conflicts, in particular, civilians, children and hostages.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This includes more than 1.4 million Palestinian refugees who have been displaced from their homes, and this Motion also makes this call.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is understandable that such conflicts can invoke strong feelings in our communities.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must take care that such overseas situations do not affect our societal harmony.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is particularly important in light of the increasing prevalence of people turning to social media, like TikTok, as a source of news which may contain misinformation and incendiary posts.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Other religious communities have also been involved in their own way.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This was observed at our local Singapore churches.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must all make continuous efforts to protect and bolster our multiracial and multi-religious society, where the necessary measures are taken by the relevant parties.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I trust in Singapore's level headedness and generosity and that our reaction will be to come together to collectively provide humanitarian support and prayer for the victims of war.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I will begin with expressing our condolences to all the innocent victims and civilian casualties in this conflict.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: My speech will touch on four key points.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Thirdly, how do we make sense of this conflict?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And lastly, what can we do in our own Singaporean way to contribute towards a resolution?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mass and social media are abuzz daily with scenes of destruction, deaths, despair and hopelessness in Gaza, as the crisis escalates and spirals out of control.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many shared that they are grappling with a range of emotions, such as anger, hurt, helplessness, and they shared their struggle to make sense of what is happening.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One Pasir Ris resident, Mr Ramos Chua, shared that it was sad and heart-wrenching to see the deaths and destruction in Gaza.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Another Pasir Ris resident, Ms Shazwani Ahmad, shared that the content on social media is devastating and it makes social media feel like a dark, black hole we cannot get out of.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many questioned the disproportionate use of force that has led us to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the size and scale of which have left us wondering how could this be happening in this day and age?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we watch the death and destruction, tolerate watching women, children and elderly fleeing for their lives, people searching frantically for their families under the rubble and see fellow humans deprive of food, water and medical supplies?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We feel utterly helpless in the face of these atrocities happening daily, as innocent lives bear the burden of collective responsibility for the attacks on 7 October.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Humanity group, Save the Children, described the living conditions in Gaza as pure horror.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many have voiced their feelings of helplessness and shared that Israel's response is disproportionate, but let the due process in international law address that, as some of our fellow Parliamentarians have mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What is clear is that many are grappling with the emotions as they feel the injustice and moral indignation, as we witness the asymmetry in military and the widespread suffering in Gaza, which sadly point towards even more deaths for civilians caught in the crossfire.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For decades, the Palestinian people have lived under difficult conditions in the occupied Palestinian territories where their basic rights have been curtailed.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The conflict had begun even before 7 October, where, for decades, the Palestinians have been subjected to systemic discrimination, abuse, restricted movements and they have endured eviction from their generational homes and witnessed expansion of illegal settlements.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The recent escalation of the conflict has no doubt made it even more inhumane for the civilians.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With no end in sight, it does not seem far-fetched to fear the worst.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As such, Mr Speaker, Sir, I stand in support of the Motion.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Singapore has remained consistent throughout the past 50 years on our position in the Middle East with regard to safeguarding humanitarian interests and upholding international law.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we continue to hope for cessation of hostilities, how do we then provide support towards a two-state solution?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What can we do, given our size and geostrategic interests?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we respond to this in a constructive way consistent with our values?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One of our volunteers in Pasir Ris, Mr Martin Modarei asked if countries like us can play a role to help the legitimate Palestinian leaders with capacity-building when the conflict winds down.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, at the international level, we need to continue to support the UN in upholding international law, just like what we did on 27 October.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Prior to this, we also voted against the illegal settlements in occupied Palestinian territory as they contravene international law, too.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Additionally, we must keep in mind our unique position.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To quote Prime Minister Lee in his speech at the joint press conference for the Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat at the Istana last Monday, "We have diplomatic relations with Israel but, at the same time, we have friendly relations with the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is in our best interest that a long-term two-state solution be diplomatically negotiated and be upheld by international law." Secondly, while we work towards an immediate humanitarian truce, we must continue to support capability-building for the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Singapore has friendly relations with the Palestinian Authority, as evident in Minister Maliki and Minister Vivian's visit to Ramallah in 2022.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is in addition to the healthcare packages during COVID-19 and customised healthcare courses and postgraduate scholarships aimed at training Palestinian policymakers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We must be ready to provide additional help to assist the Palestinians to support capability building.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I met some of the Palestinian officials on ETAP training, together with Habib Hassan, last year.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They are positive about the future and expressed appreciation at the support Singapore provides.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Thirdly, while the Israel-Hamas conflict provokes divisive views, in Singapore, as individuals, we must continue to safeguard and uphold our multiracial and multi-religious peace and harmony.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The conflict can easily be misconstrued as a religious conflict, which can quickly fan the flames of religious fervour.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The fact is, as mentioned by many Parliamentarians already, this is a complicated conflict that has been marred by history, politics, infighting, past decisions, political alliances, with many different and divisive perspectives, with different stakeholders safeguarding their own interests.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For our own peace and security, we must avoid a polarisation of views on this crisis, especially since we know it has the potential to amplify divisive lines within our society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While many societies in the world are wedged by their differences, we must stay united as a society and recognise that this is first and foremost a humanitarian crisis.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Lastly, united and together, we can mobilise our community to have a greater impact on this humanitarian crisis.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, efforts where our community comes together, regardless of race or religion, like the RLAF donation collection, Red Cross Foundation and efforts by Humanity Matters, where volunteers from different faiths come together to pack medical and relief supplies to be sent to Gaza, represent our united commitment to alleviate the humanitarian crisis.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Two weeks ago, in Pasir Ris-Punggol GRC, we organised our seventh inter-faith charity drive, aptly named, Blessings in Harmony.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It brought together the different religious organisations in Punggol such as Al-Islah Mosque, Fo Guang Shan temple, Church of the Transfiguration, amongst many others, and other volunteer organisations to work together for their beneficiaries, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In Singapore, we are indeed blessed with this harmony and we are blessed to live in harmony.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is something that we cannot take for granted.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is how we come together and respond as a united people in any time of need, including when helping others.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, my speech will touch on four points.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, to voice out the community's feelings on the Middle East issue.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, to advocate for a "humanitarian truce", and sending humanitarian aid immediately and without any obstacles to Gaza.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Lastly, what we can do, in our own way to contribute towards a lasting solution.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What more when videos on social media show that many children and families are killed in this humanitarian crisis Over decades, the Palestinians have been living in hardship in the of "occupied Palestinian territory" where their basic rights have been curtailed or neglected.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The escalation of conflict since 7 October has worsened the humanitarian crisis.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many felt that the military response caused excessive collateral damage and was an imbalanced response.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This conflict continues to injure and kill civilians regardless of age, race and religion.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We hope the UN resolution will be effective in the cessation of hostilities and providing humanitarian assistance.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is only a temporary measure, while a long-term solution is being worked out.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The fact is that these conflicts have been marred by politics, internal quarrels, past decisions, history, and different and conflicting perspectives.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This conflict is very complicated and cannot be simplified as simply differences over religion.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Those who died are regardless of age, race or religion.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is the stance that Singapore has always supported and our support for the UN resolution on 27 October reaffirms that stance.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we look forward to the cessation of hostilities, how can we provide support towards a peaceful two-state solution?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we act on this in a constructive way, in line with our values?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, a resolution can only be reached through a diplomatic solution.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Therefore, we must unite the voices to support the resolution at the UN which upholds international law.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, while we strive for the cessation of hostilities, we must continue to support the capability building efforts of the Palestinian Authority (PA).

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Singapore has a unique relationship because we have diplomatic relations with Israel and good relations with the PA.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: During my meeting with Palestinian officials who went through ETAP training in Singapore before the crisis, they shared that they had positive expectations and expressed appreciation for the support given by Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Third, while the Israel-Hamas conflict creates disunity, in Singapore, we must continue to maintain and uphold our multiracial and multi-religious peace and harmony.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We must avoid polarising views on this crisis, especially because we know it has the potential to widen the dividing cracks within our society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, when we look at the chaos around us, it is easy to be engulfed by the emotions around it.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The situation in Gaza is a humanitarian crisis, first and foremost.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The complexity in the situation makes this conflict difficult to resolve.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are ways in which Singapore can assist to alleviate the crisis.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We can only do so if we remain united together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As such, I am in support of the Motion.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The taking of innocent lives of civilians is a crime, as is the taking of innocent civilians as hostages.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: All wars are tragic and inevitably have tragic consequences on innocent lives.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Burhan Gafoor said this, following the passing of the UN resolution, "We deeply regret that this resolution has two glaring and significant omissions." "First, it makes no mention of Hamas' role in perpetrating the massive and coordinated terror attacks, which led to the brutal killing of 1,400 Israelis and others and the abduction of more than 200 hostages.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: These are acts of terror that we condemn unequivocally, and the abhorrent deeds of Hamas cannot be justified by any rationale whatsoever.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We reiterate our call for the immediate, unconditional and safe release of all civilians taken hostage." "Second, this resolution does not acknowledge Israel's legitimate right to defend its citizens and territory in compliance with international law.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As with every country, Israel has a right to defend itself from heinous terrorist attacks, to protect its people from senseless violence and to keep its territory secure." With all the discussion from fellow Members so far, I believe this House is in agreement with our Ambassador, especially as we have heard from our various Ministers as well.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our Prime Minister said this in response to media questions on the issue, "When innocent civilians suffer, infants, kids or grandparents, sometimes by side effect of military conflict, sometimes directly targeted, and in this case, what happened on 7 October when Hamas attacked Israel and launched vicious, horrible attacks against large numbers of civilians and killed 1,300 people, maybe more, mostly innocent civilians – it's horrendous.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It isn't something which could be justified by any rationale whatsoever." I agree with the Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our Minister for Law and Home Affairs had this to say on the ongoing conflict, "We need to be clear about our stance – we condemn all acts of terrorism and wanton violence.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: But we must not let these events happening externally affect the internal situation within Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We must, in Singapore, maintain our racial and religious peace." The Minister is correct and, in a subsequent interview to the media, stressed that humanitarian aid has been given by the people of Singapore across all faiths and sectors.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I quote the Minister in responding to the Humanity Matters relief effort, "Today, Humanity Matters, you look at who is contributing: Taoists, Missions, Buddhist Temples, Hindu volunteers, Muslim organisations, corporations, and of course majority of those involved are Chinese.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: This is Singapore, this is unique about Singapore – everyone comes together to help, even though they know most of the help goes towards Muslims in Gaza.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: That is what Humanity Matters' action today shows.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise," the Minister was referring to the previous day, "yesterday, Sikh temples, Hindu temples, Christian organisations, pastors, Buddhist temples, Taoist temples, they all came together, just like today.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: And I think we need to keep that spirit." It is indeed precious that Singapore has worked hard at achieving and maintaining religious and societal harmony.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore and Israel have enjoyed many decades of friendly relations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We are grateful for the support when we were in the early stages of nationhood and for assistance in training and building up our armed forces.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Today, there are strong economic ties in many areas with Israel.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Israel is a leader in the digital space.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: My fellow hon Member Mr Neil Parekh has asked about the safeguarding of our business, investment and research interests in Israel.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Wars are costly both in terms of human lives and in economic terms.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Much has been said, the current situation has immediate needs for humanitarian aid and relief.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Drawing extracts from their letters released publicly, the Mufti of Singapore wrote: "There is no place and no justification for any form of violence and brutality on civilians by anyone, including by Hamas, or in any retaliatory response.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The right to civilians to live peacefully must be protected at all times." In response, the Chief Rabbi wrote: "Our hearts and prayers are also with innocent Palestinian civilians who have lost their lives in this senseless conflict, and we do hope and pray for a peaceful and long-lasting solution to this war and a permanent peace between Israel and the Palestinian people, as elusive as it might seem at this moment."  Mr Speaker, Sir, may I say again, Singapore must do everything to preserve our unique religious and racial harmony.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The Israel-Hamas war must not be allowed to divide our society.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It is important that we stick to the correct information.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It may become necessary to combat misinformation especially on this conflict.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our political leaders need to ensure that there is a clear flow of accurate information, continue to uphold the law and to protect all races.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We are praying for the alleviation of suffering in every form, for peace to come quickly and for governments, including our Government, to intervene in appropriate ways in finding the way to peace.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Along with the other faiths, Christians in Singapore are grateful for the religious harmony we experience in Singapore and will keep playing our part to uphold this.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This is a very difficult speech for me.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Difficult, because I speak firstly as a human being, but also, equally so, as a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And so, while I express my grief and dismay at the lives lost and blood shed and homes destroyed on both sides, but especially in the Gaza Strip, where a humanitarian catastrophe is unfolding in this escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas, while I express my grief and dismay at the situation, I am also deeply cognisant about the need for me to keep my sight clearly on our national interests.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Our national interests, in a humanitarian and political crisis embroiling our brothers and sisters in another part of the world.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The right to self defence is cardinal, and sacrosanct, especially to a small state like Singapore, and Singapore's vote in favour of a cessation of hostilities, and in favour of a resolution that glaringly omits an affirmation of the right to self defence, in no way diminishes, or signals a softening of Singapore's position on our sacrosanct right to self defence.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I want to make this point, and I am glad that I have heard both the Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Deputy Prime Minister make the point, but I thought it is important that I also make the point as a backbencher, because I sense that there are some questions amongst our communities about what our vote in the UN means in terms of where we stand on our right to self defence.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: As our Ambassador to the UN Burhan Gafoor – he has been quoted many times today – put it in his intervention at the Special Session, "every country…has a right to defend itself from heinous terrorist attacks, to protect its people from senseless violence and to keep its territory secure." This is close to my heart, not only as a Singaporean, but also as a National Serviceman who has been serving in various parts of the Singapore Armed Forces.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In our training and exercises, my fellow commanders, planners and I constantly grapple with the fundamental intersection between military operations, international humanitarian law and strategic political objectives.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But we are clear, and there should be no doubt, also, I think, about where all Singaporeans should stand on this.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If we are ever called upon one day to defend ourselves, our people and our territory against the attacks of an adversary, whether state or non-state, we will do what we need to do.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And we will apply our military power to secure our existence, if that is what it takes.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: On this note, let us also be clear on another point.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Enough has been said in this House, I am not going to belabour the point.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I just want to say that I am glad to hear that we have strong consensus in this House.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Unfortunately, this amendment did not pass, with 55 votes against and 23 abstentions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, the international community is split in its views on not just the condemnation of Hamas' attacks on 7 October as acts of terror, but even the characterisation and recognition of such acts as acts of terror.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Our language and our words do matter, they matter on the international stage, they matter here at home.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The international community could not agree on the language and the words to use, but Singapore cast a strong vote in the UN in favour of that amendment proposed by Canada, and again, I am glad in this House, we have strong consensus on this basic point.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I hope, as a next stage, all Singaporeans outside of this House will be unified in our view on this point.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Because if what Hamas did on 7 October 2023 were to happen to us, we would want these acts to be recognised and condemned unequivocally as terrorist attacks.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Israel's ongoing military operations in the Gaza Strip do violate the resolution passed by the UN Special Session.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Israel has, so far, failed to take steps towards an immediate humanitarian truce, which is in contravention of the resolution.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Israel continues to prevent the full, immediate, safe, unhindered and sustained access to humanitarian aid to ensure the survival of Palestinian civilians in the Gaza Strip – again, in contravention of the resolution.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And Israel has not rescinded its order for Palestinian civilians and humanitarian workers to evacuate all areas in the Gaza Strip north of the Wadi Gaza and relocate to south Gaza – again, in contravention of the resolution.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Israel should comply fully with the UN resolution, as it should, too, with previous UN resolutions on occupied territories and settlements in the West Bank and Jerusalem.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: These are all UN resolutions that Singapore has consistently supported.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is in our interest that UN resolutions are respected and complied with, as it upholds, preserves and strengthens the multi-lateral rule-based system that is so critical to us.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Both sides of the conflict and the international community have a duty to immediately ensure basic protection and humanitarian aid for civilians.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In modern warfare, while fighting is ongoing, humanity and humanitarianism is also emphasised.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The more powerful the killing power of modern weapons, the more countries have an obligation and responsibility to uphold basic humanity.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This is the fundamental principle and spirit of today's international humanitarian law and laws of war.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: International law is crucial for Singapore as it is a small country.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The resolution also does not clearly condemn Hamas' terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: These two points touch on Singapore's core national security interest.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Therefore, we must be clear that supporting the UN resolution does not mean that Singapore's position on the right to self-defend has weakened, nor does it mean that Singapore's position on terrorism has wavered.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Singapore must strongly condemn any terrorist acts against innocent civilians.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In our country, different groups may hold strong and differing views on the Israel-Palestine issue.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But we must ensure that international events like these will not divide us.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We must maintain our hard-earned multiracial and multi religious harmony that we have enjoyed over the years.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, ultimately, I think all of us Singaporeans want peace and stability and the cessation of human suffering in this tragic conflict – not only between Israel and Hamas, but in the larger, long-standing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It requires strategic wisdom, on both sides, as Minister Vivian has said, both the Israeli political leadership, and the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Strategic wisdom, to see that attacks and counter-attacks, retaliation and retribution, will only harden hearts and harden the path to a durable, just and comprehensive negotiated two-state solution.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Restraint is the much more difficult, much less instinctive, but much more plausible path to peace.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I urge for strategic wisdom too, to see that urgent action is needed.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Urgent leadership and political organisation and action on both sides, is needed, in order for peace to have a chance, any chance.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: For the sake of millions of children, Palestinian and Israeli, Arab and Jewish, born and yet unborn, I hope both sides will do the right things, urgently, for peace.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Amid the calm of our peaceful nation, we hear the distant cries of despair from the Israel-Hamas conflict, touching our hearts with sorrow and empathy.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The humanitarian crisis unfolds not as a tally of numbers but as stories of human lives, each with a face, a name and a story.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As a father of four children, the anguish and despair engulfing the innocent children caught in this conflict resonates with me on a profound level.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a painful reminder of the cost of conflict.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We stand in solidarity with all the innocent civilians caught in this turmoil.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The lack of clean water, food, medical supplies and energy is a stark reality that demands immediate action.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore's support for UN humanitarian efforts, voiced assertively at the UN General Assembly, is underpinned by our commitment to international law and a multilateral rules-based order.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In our consistent navigation of the Israel-Palestine issue, Singapore's principled stance, through the UN resolutions, as shared by Minister Vivian, has been unflinching.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It mirrors our belief in dialogue over destruction, in peaceful negotiation over persistent conflict.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, our words and actions today reflect the humanitarian values that we hold firmly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Israel-Hamas conflict is a test of our humanitarian conscience, reminding us of the loss, pain, and hope experienced by the people of Gaza.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Every moment without humanitarian aid is a moment that steals a brighter future from the people of Gaza.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In Singapore, the Malay/Muslim community feels this sadness more keenly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our hearts break thinking about those affected, and we urge immediate humanitarian action and a peaceful solution to the ongoing situation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Two weeks ago, Minister Shanmugam held a dialogue session with more than 200 Malay/Muslim community leaders.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This dialogue has explained the Government's position and addressed some of the misinformation floating around in cyberspace.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Many appreciated the dialogue session as it gave a clearer picture of this issue.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My hope is that the Government will continue to reach out to the community, giving room to listen to their grievances, accept suggestions and feedback, and give appropriate explanations.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We should explain how Singapore, as a small country, plays a crucial role on the global stage to promote peace and humanity.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is our responsibility, to help our community better understand and prepare for future challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the past few weeks, I have had the privilege of engaging a number of youths, as well as members from M3 at Jalan Besar.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Many asked how long will this conflict last?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What does it take for this conflict to end?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And what actions will the international community take now or once the dust literally settles?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I share their sentiments and concerns and I am heartened that this issue resonates deeply with them.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Among our youths, regardless of race, the empathy and concern reflects the kind of humanity and spirit that bodes well for our future.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: While these platforms can bridge understanding and foster solidarity, they can also breed misinformation and discord.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The rapid spread of both information and misinformation has a significant impact shaping perceptions and emotions.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This underscores the need for digital literacy and critical thinking in discerning the truth amidst the sea of conflicting narratives.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Moreover, the phenomenon of doom-scrolling where individuals continuously scroll through distressing news on social media has risen.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This not only reflects our global interconnectedness, but also brings to the four mental health challenges that such crisis and their digital portrayal can precipitate.
