speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, it is imperative that we take steps to address the mental health impact by accelerating digital literacy, encouraging balance media consumption and providing mental health support through safe spaces for this course.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this vein, I am heartened to witness our Mufti being the first to provide support to the Jewish community, as well as the asatizahs, our local religious leaders such as Ustaz Mizi Wahid taking proactive steps to provide much needed holistic guidance and support for the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Their efforts are crucial in navigating the emotional and informational landscape ensuring our community remains well informed, resilient and united during this trying times.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The recent dialogue session with the Malay/Muslim leaders is a prime example.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It was a constructive discourse that reflected our unique way of addressing global issues – the Singaporean way.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am reminded of darker days when the spectre of terrorism loom large with the Jemaah Islamiyah threat.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It was a time when the fabric of our social harmony was put to the test.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Yet, Singaporeans from all walks of life, regardless of race or religion rallied together.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Religious organisations across the spectrum step forward to support the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is the hallmark of our society, a reflection of mutual respect and solidarity that binds us together.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The international law be abided with and followed through.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The loss of innocent lives in Israel and Gaza has shaken all of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am sure I speak on behalf of all Singaporeans, when I say that we feel the grief and pain of those who have lost their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the conflict in Gaza intensifies, we also watch with great concern the tremendous suffering of innocent civilians – babies, young children, the sick and the elderly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With food, water and medical aid not reaching the people, this humanitarian crisis will worsen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are already reading reports of emergency surgeries being conducted without anesthesia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is the tragic price of conflict – the loss and suffering of innocent lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is heart-wrenching and our thoughts and prayers are with all of them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The long-standing Israel-Palestine conflict is an emotive issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This latest outbreak of hostilities has led to a global rise in hate speech, crimes and attacks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked if there have been increased reports of anti-Semitic rhetoric or inter-religious disagreements in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We take firm action against acts that threaten our racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have provisions to do so in the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act and Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also have powers under the Broadcasting Act to disable access to egregious content, including those likely to cause racial or religious disharmony in Singapore, or which advocate violence or terrorism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The laws are only one part of our holistic approach to maintaining racial and religious harmony in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) regularly engage our religious and community leaders through platforms such as the National Steering Committee on Racial and Religious Harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MCCY has refreshed the 93 Racial and Religious Harmony Circles, one in each constituency, to build trust and interactions across our ethnic and religious communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MCCY also uses the Harmony Fund to support community initiatives that bring different communities together, deepen their mutual understanding and foster meaningful conversations about their commonalities and differences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Individuals who engage in offensive conduct are a minority in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Even where views on the conflict have differed, most Singaporeans have been measured and mature in our response.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We may feel deep sympathy for the civilians caught in the crossfire between Israel and Hamas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, we should be mindful that just as there are those among us who feel more deeply for the Israelis killed or abducted by Hamas, there are also many Singaporeans who are profoundly saddened by the sufferings of the Palestinian people in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We should therefore show our support and concern, in a way which does not lead to conflict and tensions among us and is not framed as a clash between religions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Whether it is an Israeli or Palestinian life, it is still a life, and we should be concerned and should be willing to give help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that Singaporeans desire to come together to show their concern and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some have applied to hold assemblies at the Speakers' Corner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi asked about applications to use the Speakers' Corner for such events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the last three years, NParks has received more than 400 applications to use the Speakers' Corner for events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The two remaining applications were for unrelated events in December 2022 and August 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Singapore Police Force (SPF) has said that public assemblies on matters related to the Israel-Hamas conflict will be prohibited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are real public safety and security concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There have been numerous incidents of violence related to the conflict in other countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Tensions are high and public demonstrations may inevitably advocate or show more sympathy for one side of the conflict or the other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can spark off incidents on the ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They also have the potential to divide us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Once we allow one event, we will have to allow others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our position is consistent with previous requests for events held outside the Speakers' Corner, where the SPF had assessed there to be a safety and security risk, such as those related to the Russia-Ukraine war.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We would have adopted the same approach if the event was held at Speakers' Corner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: NParks will continue to reject applications to use the Speakers’ Corner for such events, as long as there is a public safety and security risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are other practical and impactful avenues through which Singaporeans can show support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They may, for example, contribute to authorised fundraising activities and donation drives in support of humanitarian relief efforts, such as the fund-raising appeal by the Singapore Red Cross.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked whether there has been an increase in rhetoric or activities by extremist groups in the Southeast Asian region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hamas has issued statements calling on all Muslims to fight.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Supporters of terrorist groups like Al-Qaeda and ISIS, as well as those in Southeast Asia, have celebrated Hamas' attacks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They have called on followers to join in a wider jihad.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our security agencies are watching the situation very closely and have stepped up their alert.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Additional measures have been taken, such as enhanced security patrols at certain events and places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They should report to the authorities any suspicious behaviour or individuals whom they suspect could have been radicalised.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I call hon Members to ask their supplementary questions and clarifications, I wish to make an observation and give a reminder to this House.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I note that in the past, Members have taken this opportunity for raising points of clarification to make mini-speeches before asking their clarifications.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: With that, are there any clarifications or supplementary questions?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In that case, I will now call on Mr Vikram Nair.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It was also good to have perspectives from the backbench, from our Nominated Members and from both Opposition parties.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am heartened by the significant agreement on important matters by all parties concerned.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, the good news is I will not be using anywhere close to my full 40 minutes.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: WP has in this House clarified that their position is similar to the Government's on all the key points, including that they condemn the terrorist attacks on 7 October and recognise Israel's right of self defence.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This is important because it was not clear from their public statement, but I am grateful that the opposition has clarified that the public statement may also be modified.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I also thank Mr Leong Mun Wai and the PSP for its unequivocal support of our Motion and the Government's position on this matter.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: There is so much common ground among the speakers here that I think what I will do in this speech, in line with this Motion, is show the solidarity amongst us.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: On the first component, I think everyone who spoke understands and empathises both with the suffering of the Israeli people who are victims of the attack as well as with the plight of the Palestinian people.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think many speakers also express sympathy for the Palestinian cause, which may have been compromised, unfortunately, by this attack.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This was, I quote, by all Members in this House and all parties, and I think this is important.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Even Israel's close ally, like the US, is calling for a truce so that humanitarian supplies can reach the people.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And this builds onto the third component and some people, including Minister of State Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Mr Alex Yam, Dr Syed Harun and Mr Sharael Taha, share moving stories about the humanitarian plight and of the suffering of the civilian population.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We think it is important for the people to get access to humanitarian assistance being provided by the UN, the International Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The fourth component – condemning those responsible for the terrorist attacks and violation of international law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And the Deputy Prime Minister, Ministers, Second Ministers for Foreign Affairs, Mr Zhulkarnain, Mr Sharael Taha, have all pointed out that we have to unequivocally call out these terrorist attacks and label it as such because such attacks cannot be condoned.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And I think Mr Xie Yao Quan also highlighted that the right of self defence that correlates and arises from this is also important to recognise.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I also agree with Mr Zhulkarnain's call for both parties to facilitate investigations after the war, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It is important for both parties who wish to maintain the moral high ground to show that they intend to and respect international law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The next limb, which calls for all parties to comply with positive obligation under humanitarian law, including to ensure the safety and security of civilians, release all hostages and minimise the effects of combat on the civilian population.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The steps taken to protect the civilian population from the effects of war, I would respectfully say, include compliance with the UN resolution and facilitating humanitarian access to the agencies involved.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We then come to another point in which there was universal agreement and that is Singapore's long-standing commitment to a two-state solution.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think in my speech, I highlighted that it traces back to 1967, and I think Minister Vivian Balakrishnan also highlighted Singapore's record of votes at the UN to show how we have always been consistent with this.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We have voted to indicate also that Israel's policies of starting settlements in the Occupied Territories are illegal and we maintain this position.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We acknowledge that this policy of settlement is an obstacle to the peace process and the eventual creation of a Palestinian state.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: To Israel's credit though, they did take action to move out of the Gaza, including moving settlers out in 2005.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, in my view, this is not an insurmountable obstacle, but I think it is one that should be acknowledged.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong set out that if we are to get a peaceful resolution, Palestinians must be given a peaceful alternative to achieve statehood.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Otherwise, they may continue to support groups like Hamas that promote violence.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, for the two-state solution to become a reality, I think we have to hope that both parties and the peaceful leaders on both sides will be able to have a stronger position.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Singapore is not a big player in this situation and Singapore probably cannot individually move the needle on this, but I think many speakers have pointed out that Singapore has a good relationship with both Israel and Palestine.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And we have taken a consistent position with both.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It was also interesting to note that Dr Vivian Balakrishnan was in contact with his Egyptian counterpart, and this is to facilitate the movement of aid to the Gaza.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: These are big commitments on the part of a small country to have such high-level people involved in doing what little we can to facilitate the peace process.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Singapore has no power over either of the parties.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: All we can hope to do is lend our voice.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This means there is a real threat to Singapore's harmony that could arise from this, if we are not careful.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Minister of State Fasial also highlighted that there are calls by Hamas for regional recruitment.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Several speakers, including Mr Alex Yam, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Gerald Giam have highlighted that online misinformation targeting Singaporeans has been on the rise and Dr Wan Rizal has introduced me to a new term, "doom-scrolling", the continued consumption of negative news.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, I think, against this backdrop, it is important that all parties in this House acknowledged the need for Singapore to stay united.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Each of us, as leaders, must do our part to fight this misinformation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: While some Singaporeans have strong sentiment on the matter, we should not get these feelings divide us.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am grateful for Dr Maliki sharing of the Government's effort to fight misinformation, including with programmes in schools and I think one of the most heartening examples highlighted in this House by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, Mr Keith Chua, Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Nadia Samdin, amongst others, was position taken by two important leaders, the Chief Rabbi and the Mufti.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: He also expressed his wish for peaceful co-existence of both communities.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In response, the Chief Rabbi Mordechai Abergel said he was encouraged by the Mufti's letter and said he was grateful for Singapore's zero tolerance laws on hate speech and added that the utmost priority is for our communities to come together.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This crucial exchange sends a strong message and I hope members of both faiths and all other faiths in Singapore will take this message of solidarity and unity.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But these actions are not just from the leaders, they seem to go quite a way down.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think many of our Malay/Muslim Members of Parliament shared the efforts of the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation raising funds in Singapore, the grassroot levels but they were joined by other faiths as well as Mr Keith Chua highlighted contributions from Humanity Matters – churches, Buddhist temples, Sikh temples, Hindu temples, all coming together in support.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This, I think, is a good example of the Singapore way.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The different faiths stand in solidarity together even when there are differences amongst people in other countries that could otherwise divide us.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am grateful to this House and all its Members for standing in solidarity for peace and security in the Middle East.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any Members have any clarifications for Mr Nair?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If not, we have now come to the conclusion of the debate and I shall put the questions to the House for a decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have five amendments proposed by Mr Alex Yam.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As the House has agreed to the new part to be inserted, the consequential amendment to rename the parts will be made.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Amendment No 3 is, "In line 7, after the word 'Calls', to delete the word 'for' and insert 'on'".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Amendment No 5 is, "In line 7, to delete 'including the release of all hostages' and insert 'release all hostages and minimise the effects of combat on the civilian population'".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Original Motion as amended is now before the House.
